sentences.en: I'm Gemma Spake, and welcome back to The Psychology of Your 20s, the podcast where we talk through the biggest changes, moments, and transitions of our 20s
sentences.zh: 我是 Gemma Spake，欢迎回到《二十岁的心理学》，这是一档探讨我们二十岁时所经历的重大变化、时刻和转折的播客，

sentences.en: and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 以及这些经历对我们心理意味着什么。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到节目。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到本播客。

sentences.en: It is so great to have you here back for another episode as we, of course, break down the psychology of your 20s and beyond, your 30s, 40s, whatever age you are.
sentences.zh: 很高兴你能回来收听新的一期节目，当然，我们将继续剖析二十岁及以后——无论是三十岁、四十岁，还是任何年龄段的心理学。

sentences.en: Today we're going to talk about rituals.
sentences.zh: 今天我们要聊聊仪式感。

sentences.en: I think everybody knows how important hobbies are.
sentences.zh: 我想大家都知道爱好有多重要。

sentences.en: We need something that is outside of work, that is perhaps creative, something that you do just because you enjoy it.
sentences.zh: 我们需要一些工作之外的事情，也许是创造性的，仅仅因为喜欢而去做的事情。

sentences.en: We know that's vital.
sentences.zh: 我们知道这至关重要。

sentences.en: But rituals are this whole other category of human behavior that don't get the same credit for their importance for us emotionally.
sentences.zh: 但仪式感是人类行为中完全不同的另一类，它们在情感上的重要性往往被低估了。

sentences.en: Rituals are these things that we've been doing for hundreds of thousands of years, and they ground us, they give us meaning, they connect us to others.
sentences.zh: 仪式感是我们几十万年来一直在做的事情，它们让我们脚踏实地，赋予我们意义，并将我们与他人联系在一起。

sentences.en: And today I want to talk about specifically why we need more of them.
sentences.zh: 今天，我想专门谈谈为什么我们需要更多的仪式感。

sentences.en: For a lot of human history, society was actually structured around rituals.
sentences.zh: 在人类历史的大部分时间里，社会实际上是围绕仪式构建的。

sentences.en: There were rituals for birth and for death and for marriage and for changing seasons and for leaving home and coming home.
sentences.zh: 出生、死亡、婚姻、季节更替、离家和归家都有相应的仪式。

sentences.en: There were all these little things that we did day to day that we did every day, same time that connected us to other people, that were really organic, like we gathered wood,
sentences.zh: 我们每天在同一时间做的那些琐事，将我们与他人联系在一起，它们非常自然，比如我们一起收集木柴，

sentences.en: we prepared food in a certain way, we sang, we danced, we prayed.
sentences.zh: 以特定的方式准备食物，唱歌、跳舞、祈祷。

sentences.en: Rituals are so important for us because of their role in giving life a deeper meaning.
sentences.zh: 仪式感对我们如此重要，是因为它们在赋予生命更深层意义方面发挥了作用。

sentences.en: And the sad truth is we have fewer and fewer of those moments.
sentences.zh: 可悲的事实是，我们拥有的这类时刻越来越少了。

sentences.en: Our days are now incredibly functional and they're incredibly productive.
sentences.zh: 我们的生活现在变得极其功能化和高效。

sentences.en: Like we wake up, we check our phones, we work, exercise, eat, watch something, sleep, repeat.
sentences.zh: 比如我们醒来、看手机、工作、锻炼、吃饭、看点什么、睡觉，然后重复。

sentences.en: And a lot of what researchers are saying is that all of that has been stripped of these little moments where we actually have
sentences.zh: 研究人员指出，这一切已经剥离了那些让我们真正能够

sentences.en: to connect with what we are doing, and that is making us really, really sad and really, really isolated.
sentences.zh: 与当下所做之事产生连接的微小瞬间，这让我们感到非常、非常悲伤和孤独。

sentences.en: So today we are going to break down the psychology of rituals, what makes them so important, ways that you can reintroduce them
sentences.zh: 所以今天我们要剖析仪式的心理学，是什么让它们如此重要，以及你可以通过哪些方式将它们重新引入

sentences.en: into your life to feel that grounding, peaceful effect, and just some examples, some examples of things that you can do to actually ground yourself and connect yourself
sentences.zh: 你的生活中，去感受那种脚踏实地、宁静的效果，并提供一些例子，一些你可以做的、真正让你沉淀下来并与

sentences.en: to the deeper processes happening in your life and to something that makes your life feel a little bit more important
sentences.zh: 你生活中发生的深层过程建立连接的事情，让你的生活感觉比你现在日常生活中感受到的

sentences.en: and extraordinary than your everyday life maybe is making you feel right now.
sentences.zh: 要重要和非凡得多。

sentences.en: I'm very excited for this episode.
sentences.zh: 我对这一期节目感到非常兴奋。

sentences.en: Without further ado, let's get into the psychology of rituals.
sentences.zh: 废话不多说，让我们进入仪式的心理学。

sentences.en: So I kind of said this in the introduction, but rituals are so human.
sentences.zh: 正如我在开场白中提到的，仪式感是非常人性化的。

sentences.en: They are as human as love.
sentences.zh: 它们就像爱一样人性化。

sentences.en: They are as human as dance, as song, as sharing food.
sentences.zh: 它们就像舞蹈、歌唱、分享食物一样人性化。

sentences.en: Every single human society we know of has ritualized something, has made something meaningful through these shared,
sentences.zh: 我们所知的每一个人类社会都将某些事物仪式化了，通过这些共享的、

sentences.en: repeated practices that have been passed on through generations.
sentences.zh: 代代相传的重复实践，使某些事物变得有意义。

sentences.en: Yes, I said they help with human meaning.
sentences.zh: 是的，我说过它们有助于赋予人类意义。

sentences.en: Yes, they also help with grounding.
sentences.zh: 是的，它们也有助于让我们沉淀下来。

sentences.en: But a ritual is really what it is.
sentences.zh: 但仪式真正的本质在于，

sentences.en: It's just something that we can grab onto that is like an anchor in a storm.
sentences.zh: 它就像风暴中的锚，是我们能够紧紧抓住的东西。

sentences.en: No matter what else is happening around us, we know that this thing will always exist for us.
sentences.zh: 无论周围发生什么，我们都知道这个东西永远会为我们存在。

sentences.en: Because of that, the most common type of ritual is obviously religious.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，最常见的仪式类型显然是宗教性的。

sentences.en: Prayer is a ritual.
sentences.zh: 祈祷是一种仪式。

sentences.en: Leaving food or offerings on a shrine is a ritual.
sentences.zh: 在神龛前留下食物或供品是一种仪式。

sentences.en: Fasting is a ritual.
sentences.zh: 禁食是一种仪式。

sentences.en: That's not accidental.
sentences.zh: 这并非偶然。

sentences.en: A big reason we perform rituals is to connect to bigger beliefs, to connect to a higher power.
sentences.zh: 我们举行仪式的一个重要原因是与更宏大的信仰连接，与更高的力量连接。

sentences.en: So religion is often involved, but rituals have also always followed nature as well.
sentences.zh: 所以宗教往往涉及其中，但仪式也一直伴随着自然。

sentences.en: Like the solstices and solstice celebrations are such an amazing example of how humans like to mark different points in the season and the change between light and dark.
sentences.zh: 比如冬至和冬至庆典，就是一个绝佳的例子，展示了人类如何喜欢标记季节的不同节点，以及光明与黑暗之间的转换。

sentences.en: You know, winter solstice often is celebrated with fire and candles and feasting and gathering during the darkest part of the year.
sentences.zh: 你知道，冬至通常在一年中最黑暗的时候，通过火、蜡烛、盛宴和聚会来庆祝。

sentences.en: And summer solstice involves outdoors and flowers and bonfires and staying awake.
sentences.zh: 而夏至则涉及户外活动、鲜花、篝火和彻夜不眠。

sentences.en: And these rituals, which are deeply connected to nature and the changing of the seasons, give us a way to really engage in the natural world deeper, more profoundly.
sentences.zh: 这些与自然和季节更替紧密相连的仪式，让我们能够更深入、更深刻地参与到自然世界中。

sentences.en: It allows us to understand our place in the world and our place in nature a lot better.
sentences.zh: 它让我们更好地理解我们在世界和自然中的位置。

sentences.en: So we do it for religion.
sentences.zh: 所以我们为了宗教而做。

sentences.en: We do it for nature.
sentences.zh: 我们为了自然而做。

sentences.en: We also do it for very human things, things like graduations.
sentences.zh: 我们也为了非常人性化的事情而做，比如毕业典礼。

sentences.en: Graduations are a ritual.
sentences.zh: 毕业典礼就是一种仪式。

sentences.en: Game day activities are rituals.
sentences.zh: 比赛日的活动也是仪式。

sentences.en: Marriage contains many rituals.
sentences.zh: 婚姻包含许多仪式。

sentences.en: Walking down the aisle, the exchange of rings, wearing white, all examples.
sentences.zh: 走过红毯、交换戒指、穿白色婚纱，都是例子。

sentences.en: And then there's the smaller thing, which is the things that we do for us on the day-to-day, which I really want to talk about more in this episode.
sentences.zh: 还有一些更小的事情，就是我们每天为自己做的事情，这也是我这期节目想重点谈论的。

sentences.en: We journal.
sentences.zh: 我们写日记。

sentences.en: We do our skincare routine.
sentences.zh: 我们进行护肤流程。

sentences.en: We light a candle before bed.
sentences.zh: 我们在睡前点燃一支蜡烛。

sentences.en: We also may have birthday rituals.
sentences.zh: 我们可能还有生日仪式。

sentences.en: We, like, this is what I really want to get into.
sentences.zh: 我们，这就是我真正想深入探讨的。

sentences.en: These little things, these traditions that we create for ourselves that feel personally relevant.
sentences.zh: 这些小事，这些我们为自己创造的、感觉与个人相关的传统。

sentences.en: This is what really distinguishes a ritual from a habit, a hobby, or a custom.
sentences.zh: 这正是仪式与习惯、爱好或习俗的区别所在。

sentences.en: The major distinction is that a ritual is personally meaningful and it's symbolic.
sentences.zh: 主要的区别在于，仪式具有个人意义且具有象征性。

sentences.en: It contains meaning beyond what the action implies.
sentences.zh: 它包含的意义超出了动作本身所暗示的范畴。

sentences.en: And a lot of time, unlike hobbies, unlike customs, unlike traditions, it doesn't make practical sense.
sentences.zh: 而且很多时候，与爱好、习俗、传统不同，它在实用意义上并不合理。

sentences.en: You know, it doesn't, like, it doesn't make the tea any better to watch the leaves seep.
sentences.zh: 你知道，看着茶叶浸泡并不会让茶变得更好喝。

sentences.en: I think that's, like, an old phrase.
sentences.zh: 我想这大概是一句老话。

sentences.en: But we still do it to connect to our intention to slow down.
sentences.zh: 但我们依然这样做，是为了连接我们放慢脚步的意图。

sentences.en: Lighting a candle on a loved one's birthday, who's maybe passed, is symbolic because it's not going to bring them back, but it does allow us to feel their presence.
sentences.zh: 在已故亲人的生日点燃蜡烛，这具有象征意义，因为它不会让他们起死回生，但确实能让我们感受到他们的存在。

sentences.en: Even graduation rituals, moving your tassel from right to left when you graduate does not magically change you as a person,
sentences.zh: 即使是毕业仪式，毕业时将流苏从右拨到左，并不会神奇地改变你这个人，

sentences.en: but it's representative of this one chapter closing and this next chapter opening.
sentences.zh: 但它代表了一个篇章的结束和下一个篇章的开启。

sentences.en: All of these things, you are trying to connect with something that is not immediately available or apparent.
sentences.zh: 所有这些事情，你都是在试图与某种并非即时可见或显而易见的事物建立连接。

sentences.en: Maybe that is something spiritual.
sentences.zh: 也许那是某种精神层面的东西。

sentences.en: Maybe that is somebody who has died.
sentences.zh: 也许那是某位已经离世的人。

sentences.en: But it's also a way of connecting with your creativity, connecting with your future self, connecting with your inner child, connecting with the universe.
sentences.zh: 但这也是一种与你的创造力、与未来的自己、与内在小孩、与宇宙建立连接的方式。

sentences.en: Something that doesn't immediately feel real, a ritual is a way of making it feel tangible.
sentences.zh: 对于某种感觉不那么真实的事物，仪式是一种让它变得具体可感的方式。

sentences.en: This is the other distinction that I think is important between having rituals and having habits or hobbies.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是仪式与习惯或爱好之间另一个重要的区别。

sentences.en: Rituals aren't meant to get easier or more automatic over time.
sentences.zh: 仪式并不是为了随着时间的推移变得更容易或更自动化。

sentences.en: We perform habits repeatedly in a productive way so that they become automatic patterns and that that hopefully creates momentum
sentences.zh: 我们以高效的方式重复执行习惯，使其成为自动化的模式，希望这能产生动力，

sentences.en: and that momentum changes our behavior and that behavior changes our life.
sentences.zh: 这种动力改变我们的行为，进而改变我们的生活。

sentences.en: But rituals don't have that same requirement or goal.
sentences.zh: 但仪式没有同样的要求或目标。

sentences.en: They're meant to be quite evergreen.
sentences.zh: 它们注定是常青的。

sentences.en: They're meant to be quite emotionally fulfilling.
sentences.zh: 它们注定是情感上令人满足的。

sentences.en: Sometimes we want them to be hard.
sentences.zh: 有时我们希望它们是困难的。

sentences.en: We don't want them to get easier.
sentences.zh: 我们不希望它们变得更容易。

sentences.en: The ritual of doing a hike every year on your birthday, the ritual of speaking to your parent or your family member that you've lost before bed,
sentences.zh: 每年生日徒步的仪式，睡前与已故父母或亲人说话的仪式，

sentences.en: is it necessarily meant to get easier doing those things?
sentences.zh: 做这些事情真的注定要变得更容易吗？

sentences.en: Or is the physical, raw nature of it the point?
sentences.zh: 还是说，这种身体上的、原始的特质本身就是重点？

sentences.en: Because it shows intention.
sentences.zh: 因为它展现了意图。

sentences.en: I would say it's part of the point.
sentences.zh: 我会说这是重点的一部分。

sentences.en: So that's kind of what distinguishes rituals from habits.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是区分仪式与习惯的地方。

sentences.en: And if I haven't already convinced you, I want to talk a little bit more about why it is so important that you have something like this in your life.
sentences.zh: 如果我还没说服你，我想多谈谈为什么在生活中拥有这样的东西如此重要。

sentences.en: Why it is important for you socially, psychologically, and emotionally.
sentences.zh: 为什么它对你的社交、心理和情感如此重要。

sentences.en: The first point I want to make revolves around this paper from 2017, and it was published in the Journal of Personality Psychology.
sentences.zh: 我想提出的第一个观点围绕 2017 年的一篇论文，它发表在《人格心理学杂志》上。

sentences.en: And the research has essentially concluded, we need rituals because they are one of the easiest ways of controlling our emotions and allowing us to choose our mental state,
sentences.zh: 研究得出的基本结论是，我们需要仪式，因为它们是控制情绪并让我们选择心理状态的最简单方法之一，

sentences.en: especially when it otherwise feels like we don't have a choice.
sentences.zh: 尤其是在我们感觉自己别无选择的时候。

sentences.en: This is so important.
sentences.zh: 这一点非常重要。

sentences.en: So important when we are anxious, when we are sad, when we are unmotivated.
sentences.zh: 当我们焦虑、悲伤、缺乏动力时，这一点非常重要。

sentences.en: There is one avenue to getting out of that feeling, which is that we can try and force ourselves to not feel that way.
sentences.zh: 摆脱这种感觉有一条途径，那就是我们可以试图强迫自己不要那样去感受。

sentences.en: We can try and punish ourselves for feeling the way we don't want to feel.
sentences.zh: 我们可以因为自己产生了不想有的情绪而惩罚自己。

sentences.en: Or we can perform an action that symbolically kind of shifts the mood for us, like slowing down, making tea, humming a certain song,
sentences.zh: 或者，我们可以执行一个象征性地改变情绪的动作，比如放慢节奏、泡茶、哼唱某首歌、

sentences.en: lighting the same candle every single morning, meditating.
sentences.zh: 每天早上点燃同一支蜡烛、冥想。

sentences.en: You do those things enough times, instead of trying to force your way out of an emotion you don't want to have, the ritual cues your desired state of calm,
sentences.zh: 你做这些事情足够多次，与其试图强行摆脱某种不想有的情绪，仪式反而会触发你想要的平静、

sentences.en: of focus, of creativity, of gratitude.
sentences.zh: 专注、创造力或感恩的状态。

sentences.en: And this is so relevant when we feel out of control.
sentences.zh: 当我们感到失控时，这一点尤为重要。

sentences.en: One of the things that humans find probably not particularly difficult, like the most difficult thing, is not knowing what's going to happen next.
sentences.zh: 人类觉得最困难的事情之一，大概就是不知道接下来会发生什么。

sentences.en: Basically, the experience of uncertainty.
sentences.zh: 基本上，就是不确定性的体验。

sentences.en: Uncertainty, our brain interprets that as a thousand threats, because it's the threat of everything that could possibly happen, and everything we don't know,
sentences.zh: 不确定性，我们的大脑将其解读为成千上万种威胁，因为它是对所有可能发生的事情、所有我们未知的事情的威胁，

sentences.en: all rolled into this one catastrophic potential outcome.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都汇聚成一个潜在的灾难性结果。

sentences.en: Uncertainty represents every single bad thing that could possibly occur.
sentences.zh: 不确定性代表了所有可能发生的坏事。

sentences.en: So it's just naturally, intensely overwhelming.
sentences.zh: 所以它自然而然地让人感到极其压抑。

sentences.en: When we perform rituals, even superstitions, which is a specific kind of ritual,
sentences.zh: 当我们执行仪式，甚至是迷信（这是一种特殊的仪式）时，

sentences.en: we insert something that we can control.
sentences.zh: 我们植入了一些我们可以控制的东西。

sentences.en: We insert something that we know will be certain, that we know will always be something that we can do from a place of calm, rationality, and intention.
sentences.zh: 我们植入了一些我们知道是确定的东西，我们知道这永远是可以从平静、理性和意图出发去做的事情。

sentences.en: For example, there has been extensive research in sports psychology that shows matter-of-factly that athletes who perform certain rituals
sentences.zh: 例如，运动心理学中有大量的研究明确表明，那些在每场比赛、每场对决、每次训练前执行特定仪式的运动员，

sentences.en: before every game, before every match, before every practice, perform better because they are able to control their emotional state.
sentences.zh: 表现得更好，因为他们能够控制自己的情绪状态。

sentences.en: Rafael Nadal is a great example, famous tennis player.
sentences.zh: 拉斐尔·纳达尔就是一个很好的例子，著名的网球运动员。

sentences.en: He had 19 rituals, exactly 19 rituals that he performed before every single match.
sentences.zh: 他有 19 个仪式，确切地说是 19 个他在每场比赛前都会执行的仪式。

sentences.en: And he said this was his way of ordering his surroundings to match the order that he sought in his head so that he could perform the best that he could.
sentences.zh: 他说这是他整理周围环境以匹配他脑海中寻求的秩序的方式，这样他才能发挥出最佳水平。

sentences.en: And I think that's the most brilliant way of putting it.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是最精彩的表达方式。

sentences.en: They create order that feels intentional.
sentences.zh: 它们创造了感觉上有意图的秩序。

sentences.en: There's this really fascinating study that was published in 2015.
sentences.zh: 有一项非常迷人的研究发表于 2015 年。

sentences.en: It's a bit of a long one, but it's a really good one, so just bear with me.
sentences.zh: 内容有点长，但非常棒，请耐心听我说。

sentences.en: It was a study titled The Effects of Anxiety on Spontaneous Ritualized Behavior.
sentences.zh: 这项研究的标题是《焦虑对自发仪式化行为的影响》。

sentences.en: And the researchers wanted to see whether anxiety changes the way people actually move and behave in their bodies.
sentences.zh: 研究人员想看看焦虑是否会改变人们在身体上的实际移动和行为方式。

sentences.en: And the way they did this was that they split participants into two groups.
sentences.zh: 他们的方法是将参与者分成两组。

sentences.en: One group was a low-anxiety group.
sentences.zh: 一组是低焦虑组。

sentences.en: One group was a high-anxiety group.
sentences.zh: 一组是高焦虑组。

sentences.en: In the high-anxiety group, they said, we want you to prepare a speech.
sentences.zh: 在高焦虑组中，他们说，我们希望你准备一场演讲。

sentences.en: You're going to deliver this speech to a panel of experts.
sentences.zh: 你要向专家小组发表这段演讲。

sentences.en: And the speech is about a random decorative object.
sentences.zh: 演讲的内容是关于一个随意的装饰品。

sentences.en: And you have like an hour or something.
sentences.zh: 你大概有一个小时左右的时间。

sentences.en: In the low-anxiety group, they were like, we just want you to prepare a description.
sentences.zh: 在低焦虑组中，他们被告知，我们只是想让你准备一份描述。

sentences.en: You don't have to present it to anyone.
sentences.zh: 你不需要向任何人展示它。

sentences.en: It's just a little task.
sentences.zh: 这只是一个小任务。

sentences.en: Whilst they were preparing for either task, the researchers tracked the participants' movements.
sentences.zh: 当他们准备这两项任务时，研究人员追踪了参与者的动作。

sentences.en: What they found was that when the students who were in the high-anxiety condition, when they were stressed, they were picking up this object and they were handling it a lot more.
sentences.zh: 他们发现，当处于高焦虑状态的学生感到压力时，他们会拿起这个物体并更多地摆弄它。

sentences.en: And they were often moving it in a really repetitive pattern compared to the relaxed group.
sentences.zh: 与放松组相比，他们经常以一种非常重复的模式移动它。

sentences.en: The physical data they got basically showed that repetitive motor patterns aligned with spikes in heart rate.
sentences.zh: 他们获得的生理数据基本上显示，重复的运动模式与心率的激增是一致的。

sentences.en: So essentially, the more anxious you become, the more you are going to try and ground yourself in something that you feel that you can control, such as, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以本质上，你变得越焦虑，你就越会试图在某些你觉得可以控制的事情上找到立足点，比如，你知道，

sentences.en: turning over a little thing in your hand over and over again, like kind of bouncing your knee.
sentences.zh: 在手中反复翻转一个小东西，或者像抖腿一样。

sentences.en: As our brain experiences this spike in anxiety, what we want most of all is something that's familiar.
sentences.zh: 当我们的大脑经历这种焦虑激增时，我们最想要的是熟悉的东西。

sentences.en: And we want an ordered pattern of behavior that makes whatever environment that we are in more predictable.
sentences.zh: 我们想要一种有序的行为模式，使我们所处的任何环境都更具可预测性。

sentences.en: I think that gives us a really, like probably one of the best ways of understanding why engaging in rituals can feel so grounding and why we need them now more than ever.
sentences.zh: 我认为这为我们提供了一种理解为什么参与仪式会让人感到如此踏实，以及为什么我们现在比以往任何时候都更需要它们的方法，这可能是最好的方法之一。

sentences.en: The level of uncertainty in this world is overwhelming.
sentences.zh: 这个世界的不确定性水平令人难以承受。

sentences.en: There's so little in our lives, well, just in the world around us that we can directly control.
sentences.zh: 我们的生活中，或者说我们周围的世界中，几乎没有什么我们可以直接控制的。

sentences.en: And it's very easy for that to make us very hopeless and depressed.
sentences.zh: 这很容易让我们感到绝望和沮丧。

sentences.en: And I think rituals might not save the world, but they will save your sanity.
sentences.zh: 我认为仪式可能无法拯救世界，但它们能拯救你的理智。

sentences.en: And that's enough.
sentences.zh: 这就足够了。

sentences.en: And the sad thing is that despite knowing the deep psychological importance of these things that we do for ourselves, of these rituals, we have fewer and fewer of them.
sentences.zh: 可悲的是，尽管我们知道这些我们为自己所做的事情，即这些仪式，具有深远的心理重要性，但我们拥有的仪式却越来越少。

sentences.en: There are all these psychologists that basically say the reason we're lonely, the reason that we lack meaning,
sentences.zh: 有许多心理学家基本上说，我们感到孤独、缺乏意义的原因，

sentences.en: the reason that we're depressed is a loss of ritualized activities in society.
sentences.zh: 我们感到沮丧的原因，是社会中仪式化活动的缺失。

sentences.en: Because as much as they connect us to ourselves and they give us certainty, they also connect us to other people.
sentences.zh: 因为它们在让我们与自己建立联系并给予我们确定性的同时，也将我们与他人联系在一起。

sentences.en: Ritualistic behavior has this really crucial role to play in social bonding.
sentences.zh: 仪式化行为在社会凝聚力中起着至关重要的作用。

sentences.en: Group rituals in particular, like they indicate, we don't have any anymore really, but they indicate that members were like-minded, we share certain values,
sentences.zh: 群体仪式尤其如此，它们表明——虽然我们现在几乎没有了——成员们志同道合，我们分享某些价值观，

sentences.en: we're all doing this thing, we all care about this thing.
sentences.zh: 我们都在做这件事，我们都关心这件事。

sentences.en: Festivals are like an amazing example.
sentences.zh: 节日就是一个很好的例子。

sentences.en: Holidays are an amazing example.
sentences.zh: 假期就是一个很好的例子。

sentences.en: Ritualistic chants have been shown, for example, to make football fans feel more connected, which is why every team has one.
sentences.zh: 例如，仪式性的口号已被证明能让足球迷感到更紧密的联系，这就是为什么每支球队都有一个口号。

sentences.en: Like that is the reason your football team has a chant is psychological.
sentences.zh: 你的足球队有口号的原因就是心理层面的。

sentences.en: There's just so many reasons why a ritual helps people unite around this core common thing that they all get to reach out and touch and say,
sentences.zh: 仪式能帮助人们围绕一个他们都能触及并表达的核心共同点团结起来，原因有很多，

sentences.en: we're going to do this and we care about this together.
sentences.zh: 我们一起做这件事，我们一起关心这件事。

sentences.en: The more we lose those things, the more we lose a crucial ability, not just to self-regulate, but to co-regulate.
sentences.zh: 我们失去这些东西越多，我们失去的一种关键能力就越多，不仅是自我调节的能力，还有共同调节的能力。

sentences.en: I want to talk about this, what they call detraditionalization or deritualization, a little bit more.
sentences.zh: 我想多谈谈这个，他们所说的去传统化或去仪式化。

sentences.en: We're going to take a short break and then when we return, we'll get into it.
sentences.zh: 我们要休息一下，回来后再深入探讨。

sentences.en: I've been approaching my health really differently this year.
sentences.zh: 今年我对待健康的方式非常不同。

sentences.en: I used to be really focused on maximizing and doing more.
sentences.zh: 我过去非常专注于最大化和做更多的事情。

sentences.en: And now I'm just realizing that if I listen to what my body needs, I perform way better.
sentences.zh: 现在我意识到，如果我倾听身体的需求，我的表现会好得多。

sentences.en: And that's why I am obsessed with my Whoop.
sentences.zh: 这就是我沉迷于 Whoop 的原因。

sentences.en: Truly, you guys, you know,
sentences.zh: 真的，伙计们，你们知道，

sentences.en: I'm such a data and information driven person.
sentences.zh: 我是一个非常注重数据和信息的人。

sentences.en: And I love opening my Whoop app and seeing how my sleep, my stress, my strain is correlating with my mood, with my running performance, with how I'm just feeling day to day.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢打开 Whoop 应用程序，看看我的睡眠、压力、劳累程度如何与我的情绪、跑步表现以及我每天的感觉相关联。

sentences.en: I'm not an elite athlete by any means, but I do really benefit.
sentences.zh: 我绝不是精英运动员，但我确实受益匪浅。

sentences.en: And I also just really enjoy knowing more about my body.
sentences.zh: 而且我也真的很喜欢更多地了解我的身体。

sentences.en: And Whoop also gives me these actionable, personalized insights that have made me more intentional and meant that I make
sentences.zh: Whoop 还为我提供了这些可操作的、个性化的见解，使我更有意图，意味着我能

sentences.en: smarter decisions day to day about what I need rather than just putting my foot on the gas and just going, going, going, going.
sentences.zh: 每天做出更明智的决定，了解我需要什么，而不是仅仅踩下油门，不停地、不停地前进。

sentences.en: So the world is losing its rituals.
sentences.zh: 所以世界正在失去它的仪式。

sentences.en: This we know.
sentences.zh: 这一点我们知道。

sentences.en: We know this from our experience.
sentences.zh: 我们从经验中知道这一点。

sentences.en: We also know because it's been extensively detailed and there's a really amazing book on this that was published in 2022 by the Korean German author Byung Chul Han.
sentences.zh: 我们也知道这一点，因为它已被广泛详细说明，而且韩裔德国作家韩炳哲（Byung-Chul Han）在 2022 年出版了一本关于此的非常棒的书。

sentences.en: And he basically said what I've already said, we've lost rituals.
sentences.zh: 他基本上说了我已经说过的话，我们已经失去了仪式。

sentences.en: That's making us sad.
sentences.zh: 这让我们感到悲伤。

sentences.en: But he was like, why?
sentences.zh: 但他问，为什么？

sentences.en: Why has this happened?
sentences.zh: 为什么会发生这种情况？

sentences.en: And that's where I think his work was very interesting.
sentences.zh: 我认为他的作品在这一点上非常有趣。

sentences.en: The first thing he says is religion is a less deeply ingrained part of our daily life.
sentences.zh: 他说的第一件事是宗教在我们日常生活中不再是根深蒂固的一部分。

sentences.en: Our life is less structured around prayer, church, those sorts of things.
sentences.zh: 我们的生活不再围绕祈祷、教堂这类事情来构建。

sentences.en: The amount of people who would say I am religious, I follow a religion has halved.
sentences.zh: 自称有宗教信仰、追随某种宗教的人数已经减半。

sentences.en: This has been the biggest driver towards that thing I mentioned before,
sentences.zh: 这是导致我之前提到的那件事的最大驱动力，

sentences.en: detraditionalization.
sentences.zh: 去传统化。

sentences.en: In the past 40,
sentences.zh: 在过去的 40、

sentences.en: 50 years, the level of inherited social traditions or cultural traditions we have been doing has rapidly decreased because a lot of people are moving away from
sentences.zh: 50 年里，我们所继承的社会传统或文化传统的水平迅速下降，因为许多人正在远离

sentences.en: major institutions like the church.
sentences.zh: 像教会这样的大型机构。

sentences.en: Is that a good thing or a bad thing?
sentences.zh: 这是一件好事还是坏事？

sentences.en: If we're looking through the lens of rituals alone, it's not great.
sentences.zh: 如果我们仅仅通过仪式的视角来看，这并不好。

sentences.en: And it's not great because those rituals haven't been replaced.
sentences.zh: 这并不好，因为那些仪式并没有被取代。

sentences.en: Maybe some of those things needed to go, but there's been nothing that's kind of filled the hole left by these things that we did as collectives.
sentences.zh: 也许其中一些事情确实需要消失，但没有什么东西填补了我们作为集体所做的这些事情留下的空白。

sentences.en: That is the first reason that we are losing our rituals.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们失去仪式的第一个原因。

sentences.en: Less people are religious.
sentences.zh: 信教的人少了。

sentences.en: The second point this author makes is about money.
sentences.zh: 这位作者提出的第二点是关于金钱。

sentences.en: Rituals inherently feel good.
sentences.zh: 仪式本质上让人感觉良好。

sentences.en: It feels good to do things over and over again for you symbolically.
sentences.zh: 反复做一些具有象征意义的事情会让你感觉良好。

sentences.en: And companies have realized that they can benefit from that good feeling financially if they can bottle that feeling up.
sentences.zh: 公司已经意识到，如果他们能将这种感觉装瓶，他们就能从这种良好的感觉中获得经济利益。

sentences.en: So they've commodified, they've commercialized and they've turned rituals into consumer experiences.
sentences.zh: 所以他们将仪式商品化、商业化，并将其变成了消费体验。

sentences.en: Instead of being something that you do with lots of people and you do symbolically, they've become something that you can buy.
sentences.zh: 它们不再是你与许多人一起做的、具有象征意义的事情，而变成了你可以购买的东西。

sentences.en: You know, getting sunlight first thing in the morning is a ritual to like wake yourself up has turned into a red light mask.
sentences.zh: 你知道，清晨晒太阳作为一种唤醒自己的仪式，已经变成了红光面罩。

sentences.en: Carefully like brewing and laboring over your coffee that you're making for your family has turned into like buying a trending drink from like Starbucks or somewhere.
sentences.zh: 精心冲泡和制作给家人喝的咖啡，已经变成了从星巴克或其他地方购买流行饮料。

sentences.en: Christmas and holiday rituals that used to be small and inexpensive, like putting sweets or coal in a stocking, has now turned into dozens of elaborate gifts,
sentences.zh: 曾经小巧且廉价的圣诞节和节日仪式，比如在袜子里放糖果或煤炭，现在已经变成了几十种精致的礼物，

sentences.en: theme decorations every single year.
sentences.zh: 每年都有主题装饰。

sentences.en: Small things that used to be purely symbolic and they were meant to be fun.
sentences.zh: 曾经纯粹具有象征意义且旨在带来乐趣的小事，

sentences.en: It now feels like sometimes there's some pressure around them and that they've been perhaps
sentences.zh: 现在有时感觉周围有一些压力，而且它们可能已经被

sentences.en: hijacked and made into these like cheap and easy dopamine pathways because companies have
sentences.zh: 劫持并变成了这些廉价且容易的多巴胺途径，因为公司已经

sentences.en: taken the essence of what a ritual is and found a way to make a lot of money out of it by making it feel like this is something we absolutely need in that form.
sentences.zh: 抓住了仪式的本质，并找到了一种通过让它感觉像是我们绝对需要的形式来从中赚取大量金钱的方法。

sentences.en: Remember the thing we said at the beginning, rituals aren't necessarily meant to be easy.
sentences.zh: 记住我们开头说的话，仪式并不一定非要容易。

sentences.en: They're not meant to be as easy as buying something.
sentences.zh: 它们不应该像买东西那么容易。

sentences.en: They're not meant to always be pleasurable.
sentences.zh: 它们不一定总是令人愉快的。

sentences.en: Rituals occur because they create depth and connection.
sentences.zh: 仪式的出现是因为它们创造了深度和联系。

sentences.en: So the more we turn rituals into something that we need to buy a specific product for
sentences.zh: 所以，我们越是把仪式变成我们需要购买特定产品的东西，

sentences.en: or something that we need to have a specific item for or something that we need to pay to perform,
sentences.zh: 或者我们需要拥有特定物品的东西，或者我们需要付费才能执行的东西，

sentences.en: the worse our general emotional wellbeing is going to be because we are losing something that was otherwise completely free, which is small symbolic acts, small things,
sentences.zh: 我们的整体情绪健康就会越差，因为我们正在失去一些原本完全免费的东西，即微小的象征性行为、小事，

sentences.en: small touchstones that you do every day, you know, touching the pole of your front porch before you leave for work or for school, really like having silence in the morning,
sentences.zh: 你每天做的微小触点，你知道，在去上班或上学之前触摸一下前廊的柱子，或者在早上保持安静，

sentences.en: all these little things that it's like, well, now I can like, if I can make money off of that feeling, there are a lot of people who are going to, who are going to do that.
sentences.zh: 所有这些小事，就像是，好吧，现在我可以，如果我能从那种感觉中赚钱，会有很多人愿意这样做。

sentences.en: There's also another point he makes, which is that we have fewer and fewer rituals because we are less connected with nature.
sentences.zh: 他还提出了另一点，即我们拥有的仪式越来越少，因为我们与自然的联系减少了。

sentences.en: This is probably my favorite explanation.
sentences.zh: 这可能是我最喜欢的解释。

sentences.en: 66% of the world's population lives in urban areas.
sentences.zh: 世界上 66% 的人口居住在城市地区。

sentences.en: Historically, many of our rituals were organized around the natural world.
sentences.zh: 历史上，我们的许多仪式都是围绕自然世界组织的。

sentences.en: The changing of the seasons is one of them.
sentences.zh: 季节更替就是其中之一。

sentences.en: Solstices, as I mentioned, is another, but harvests, the phases of the moon, planting and gathering food, winter, the transition from light into dark, dark into light.
sentences.zh: 正如我提到的，至日是另一个，还有收获、月相、种植和采集食物、冬天、从光明到黑暗、从黑暗到光明的过渡。

sentences.en: As our lives have moved more indoors, specifically, what he says is that the seasons have mattered less because we are able to basically erase natural cycles in our everyday life.
sentences.zh: 随着我们的生活更多地转移到室内，他具体说的是，季节变得不那么重要了，因为我们基本上能够在日常生活中抹去自然周期。

sentences.en: If you go from work to home, it might be the same temperature everywhere, but the journey in between.
sentences.zh: 如果你从工作场所回到家，到处可能都是一样的温度，但中间的旅程呢。

sentences.en: You're not as connected with what's happening in the natural world around you.
sentences.zh: 你与周围自然世界发生的事情联系得不够紧密。

sentences.en: Winter, for example, used to be this reason for us to slow down because it's cold outside, we can't work, the harvest isn't, like the food isn't being produced.
sentences.zh: 例如，冬天过去是我们放慢脚步的理由，因为外面很冷，我们不能工作，收获没有，食物没有生产。

sentences.en: Now, we're expected to really maintain the same pace continuously, regardless of how sad you
sentences.zh: 现在，我们被期望持续保持相同的节奏，无论你感到多么悲伤，

sentences.en: Psychologically, it's because like a ritual has to feel important to you.
sentences.zh: 从心理学上讲，是因为仪式必须让你觉得很重要。

sentences.en: It has to feel like I'm doing this for something beyond just me.
sentences.zh: 它必须让你觉得“我做这件事不仅仅是为了我自己”。

sentences.en: Like otherwise you will never do it.
sentences.zh: 否则你永远不会去做。

sentences.en: This is what creates this thing we know as intrinsic motivation.
sentences.zh: 这就是创造我们所知的“内在动机”的东西。

sentences.en: A ritual that somebody else gives you that doesn't feel personally significant is going to feel like a chore.
sentences.zh: 如果别人给你的仪式让你觉得没有个人意义，那就会感觉像是一种苦差事。

sentences.en: That is why a lot of people kind of are walking away from like the traditional idea of religion because it's like,
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么很多人开始远离传统的宗教观念，因为他们会觉得：

sentences.en: well, this ritual of prayer of this ritual of whatever, like doesn't feel important to me.
sentences.zh: “嗯，这个祈祷仪式或那个仪式，对我来说没什么意义。”

sentences.en: You need to do something that offers a metaphor for your life in a way that maybe only you can understand.
sentences.zh: 你需要做一些能为你的生活提供隐喻的事情，而且这种方式可能只有你自己能理解。

sentences.en: And that is going to mean that you feel dedicated to this ritual and you're going to want to keep doing it.
sentences.zh: 这意味着你会对这个仪式感到专注，并且会想要一直坚持下去。

sentences.en: So I thought I'd finish this episode by just giving you some examples, giving you some examples for the situations that you are in.
sentences.zh: 所以我打算在这一集的结尾，给你举一些例子，针对你所处的不同情况提供一些参考。

sentences.en: An easy one is, if you don't have an end of workday ritual, you need one.
sentences.zh: 一个简单的例子是：如果你没有下班仪式，你需要一个。

sentences.en: Always changing your clothes after work, writing your to-do list for the next morning, having a shower.
sentences.zh: 下班后换衣服、写下第二天的待办事项清单、洗个澡。

sentences.en: Vital for being like, I'm distinguishing this area from my life from this area.
sentences.zh: 这对于区分生活中的这一部分和那一部分至关重要。

sentences.en: Maybe you need a ritual for getting into a creative mindset.
sentences.zh: 也许你需要一个进入创造性思维的仪式。

sentences.en: Before you paint, before you study, before you work, before you write, perhaps you clear your desk.
sentences.zh: 在你绘画、学习、工作或写作之前，也许你可以先清理桌面。

sentences.en: That metaphor for a blank slate.
sentences.zh: 那是“从零开始”的隐喻。

sentences.en: Maybe you make a specific blend of tea.
sentences.zh: 也许你可以冲泡一种特定的茶。

sentences.en: Maybe you dance for three minutes.
sentences.zh: 也许你可以跳三分钟舞。

sentences.en: Whatever it is.
sentences.zh: 无论是什么。

sentences.en: I've become really obsessed with reading about the rituals of incredibly creative people.
sentences.zh: 我最近非常沉迷于阅读那些极具创造力的人的仪式。

sentences.en: And I think it's a really great rabbit hole to go down.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个非常值得深入探索的领域。

sentences.en: But some of the interesting ones was like Beethoven.
sentences.zh: 其中一些有趣的例子，比如贝多芬。

sentences.en: He personally counted out 60 coffee beans every single morning before he started to write.
sentences.zh: 他每天早上开始写作前，都会亲自数出60颗咖啡豆。

sentences.en: A lot of poets and authors notoriously often do a lot of walking.
sentences.zh: 许多诗人和作家众所周知经常会进行大量的步行。

sentences.en: Dr. Seuss would wear a specific hat when he was feeling uninspired.
sentences.zh: 苏斯博士在感到灵感枯竭时会戴上一顶特定的帽子。

sentences.en: A lot of creative people, their avenue to feeling productive and to feeling like they are ready to make is through something that has absolutely nothing to do with making.
sentences.zh: 许多有创造力的人，他们获得生产力感并感觉自己准备好创作的途径，是通过一些与创作完全无关的事情。

sentences.en: Their avenue to getting in touch with this part of themselves is something that often feels completely pointless.
sentences.zh: 他们与内心这部分建立联系的途径，往往是一些看起来完全毫无意义的事情。

sentences.en: Why wear a funny hat?
sentences.zh: 为什么要戴一顶滑稽的帽子？

sentences.en: Why count 60 beans?
sentences.zh: 为什么要数60颗豆子？

sentences.en: Because it's like this is a metaphor.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一种隐喻。

sentences.en: This is symbolic for me for the kind of mindset that I want to be in.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说象征着我想要进入的那种心态。

sentences.en: So a creative ritual is another one.
sentences.zh: 所以，创造性仪式是另一种仪式。

sentences.en: You might also create rituals around relationships.
sentences.zh: 你也可以围绕人际关系创造仪式。

sentences.en: Maybe you and your housemate cook together every Friday.
sentences.zh: 也许你和室友每周五一起做饭。

sentences.en: Me and my boyfriend have a bunch of rituals.
sentences.zh: 我和我男朋友有很多仪式。

sentences.en: We do like a movie night once a month.
sentences.zh: 我们每个月会有一个电影之夜。

sentences.en: Me and my long distance friends as well.
sentences.zh: 我和我的异地朋友也是如此。

sentences.en: Every night that we see, like any city that we see each other in, after not seeing each other for a while, we always go and get Italian.
sentences.zh: 每次我们在某个城市见面，在很久没见之后，我们总是会去吃意大利菜。

sentences.en: I was actually saying this to somebody before, the ritual that me and my boyfriend are really enjoying right now is that we've, this is so weird, but we found this potato.
sentences.zh: 我之前其实跟别人说过，我和我男朋友现在非常享受的一个仪式是——这听起来很奇怪，但我们发现了一个土豆。

sentences.en: And this is strange.
sentences.zh: 这很奇怪。

sentences.en: Like again, it doesn't have to matter to anybody but you, but we found this potato and our little ritual has been like hiding it around the house.
sentences.zh: 再次强调，它不需要对任何人有意义，只需要对你有意义。我们发现了这个土豆，我们的小仪式就是把它藏在房子的各个角落。

sentences.en: And it's currently missing.
sentences.zh: 它现在不见了。

sentences.en: So it's like rotting somewhere in our home.
sentences.zh: 所以它可能正在我们家里的某个地方腐烂。

sentences.en: Somebody has hit it too well, but like it would show up in the shampoo bottle and like show up in like a shoe or like in like your headphone case.
sentences.zh: 有人把它藏得太好了，它会出现在洗发水瓶子里，或者出现在鞋子里，或者耳机盒里。

sentences.en: And it is this thing of like,
sentences.zh: 这就像是，

sentences.en: Tom's at work, I'm at home.
sentences.zh: 汤姆在上班，我在家。

sentences.en: And then I find the potato and I'm like, oh my God, I'm thinking about you.
sentences.zh: 然后我发现了那个土豆，我就想：噢天哪，我在想你。

sentences.en: And then I go to the gym and he's, he's at home and it's like, oh, the potato.
sentences.zh: 然后我去健身房，他在家，他就会想：噢，那个土豆。

sentences.en: And it's like, what does a potato mean?
sentences.zh: 这就像是，土豆意味着什么？

sentences.en: Nothing.
sentences.zh: 什么都不意味着。

sentences.en: But there's a meaning applied to it, which is I hid this potato for you.
sentences.zh: 但被赋予了意义，那就是：我为你藏了这个土豆。

sentences.en: I participated in the ritual of being like, I'm going to make space in my day to pick up this rotting vegetable and hide it because that's meaningful.
sentences.zh: 我参与了这个仪式，就像是：我会在忙碌的一天中腾出时间，拿起这个腐烂的蔬菜并把它藏起来，因为这很有意义。

sentences.en: So maybe you and your partner, if you're feeling like you've lost a spark, you need to go to the grocery store and get a potato.
sentences.zh: 所以也许你和你的伴侣，如果觉得失去了火花，你们需要去杂货店买个土豆。

sentences.en: It's a, it's a specific like mini gem potato as well.
sentences.zh: 最好是那种特定的迷你小土豆。

sentences.en: If you really want to do this by the book.
sentences.zh: 如果你真的想按部就班地做的话。

sentences.en: And then of course you can do rituals around solitude, which are probably the most important.
sentences.zh: 当然，你也可以围绕独处进行仪式，这可能是最重要的。

sentences.en: And the first thing you do every holiday morning, or like the first day of every holiday is you go for a walk by yourself.
sentences.zh: 比如每个假期早上的第一件事，或者每个假期的第一天，你独自去散步。

sentences.en: Every Sunday, you do five pages in your journal.
sentences.zh: 每个周日，你在日记里写五页纸。

sentences.en: Every Saturday morning, the first thing you do is go and watch the sunset.
sentences.zh: 每个周六早上，你做的第一件事就是去看日落。

sentences.en: Maybe you do a solo trip every year on your birthday, something like that.
sentences.zh: 也许你每年生日都会进行一次独自旅行，诸如此类。

sentences.en: I also think we need solo rituals around achievement as well.
sentences.zh: 我也认为我们需要围绕成就感建立独处仪式。

sentences.en: I think we are often terrible at not marking achievement the way we don't mark years of our lives.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们往往很不擅长去标记成就，就像我们不标记生命中的岁月一样。

sentences.en: When you've worked really hard on something for months, it's the habit of just being like,
sentences.zh: 当你为某件事辛苦工作了几个月，习惯性地会觉得，

sentences.en: I've sent that off.
sentences.zh: 我把它发出去了。

sentences.en: It's done.
sentences.zh: 完成了。

sentences.en: And I'm so relieved that you don't celebrate it is very much ingrained in us.
sentences.zh: 而我们内心深处根深蒂固的习惯，就是因为感到如释重负，所以反而不去庆祝它。

sentences.en: And I think instead of doing that, mark that achievement, mark moments in your life, go and buy yourself some fresh flowers, take yourself out for lunch.
sentences.zh: 我觉得与其那样，不如去标记那个成就，标记你生活中的时刻，去给自己买束鲜花，带自己出去吃顿午餐。

sentences.en: Every time you meet a really important deadline.
sentences.zh: 每次你赶上一个非常重要的截止日期时。

sentences.en: One of our researchers, Libby is currently doing her PhD thesis.
sentences.zh: 我们的一位研究员Libby目前正在写她的博士论文。

sentences.en: And she gave me this amazing example, which is that each time she finishes a chapter of her thesis, she takes the afternoon off and she gets her nails done.
sentences.zh: 她给了我一个很棒的例子，她说每次写完论文的一章，她就会给自己放半天假，去做个美甲。

sentences.en: Not only does she mark the occasion, but she was saying she gets a different pattern every single time.
sentences.zh: 她不仅是为了纪念这个时刻，而且她说每次做的图案都不一样。

sentences.en: So every single chapter of her thesis has had its own set of nails that has written it.
sentences.zh: 所以她论文的每一章都有属于它自己的美甲款式。

sentences.en: I feel like that, isn't that such a great idea?
sentences.zh: 我觉得这主意太棒了，不是吗？

sentences.en: And like, I just think that's a beautiful way of being like, look at my progress.
sentences.zh: 我真的觉得这是一种很美的方式，就像是在说，看看我的进步。

sentences.en: Look at how I'm marking time.
sentences.zh: 看看我是如何标记时间的。

sentences.en: Look at how I'm marking my own achievement rather than just allowing
sentences.zh: 看看我是如何标记自己的成就的，而不是任由

sentences.en: a year of my life or an event in my life or an activity in my life or a relationship just be this
sentences.zh: 我生命中的一年，或者生命中的某个事件、某项活动、某段关系，仅仅变成

sentences.en: like big clump of years or this big clump of moments when nothing distinguishes one moment from the next and nothing feels intentional.
sentences.zh: 一大堆年份，或者一大堆时刻，没有任何时刻能与众不同，也没有任何事情让人感觉是有意为之的。

sentences.en: I'm just trying to live through this moment.
sentences.zh: 我只是在努力度过这一刻。

sentences.en: I feel like you have plenty of ideas to go off of here.
sentences.zh: 我觉得你这里有很多可以借鉴的想法。

sentences.en: And I would love if you shared any that you personally have, if you and your partner also hide potatoes from each other, I will personally send you a signed potato.
sentences.zh: 如果你有什么个人的想法，我很乐意你分享出来。如果你和你的伴侣也会互相藏土豆，我会亲自寄给你一个签名土豆。

sentences.en: That sounds like too big of a promise, but no, I want to know if you have something silly like that.
sentences.zh: 这听起来像是个太大的承诺，但不是的，我只是想知道你是否有类似这样有趣的小习惯。

sentences.en: And leave a comment on Spotify or DM me and I'll make a big master list of ritual ideas
sentences.zh: 在Spotify上留言或者私信我，我会整理出一份仪式感点子的大清单，

sentences.en: that if you're feeling like you're lacking, you can maybe go and steal something from that liSt.
sentences.zh: 如果你觉得生活缺乏仪式感，或许可以从那份清单里偷学一两招。

sentences.en: I hope I've made a good argument for why you need more rituals, what we've lost in society by removing these spiritual moments, these traditional moments, these rites of passage.
sentences.zh: 希望我刚才关于为什么你需要更多仪式感，以及我们因失去这些精神时刻、传统时刻和人生转折点而在社会中失去了什么的论述，能让你信服。

sentences.en: I feel like we'd all be a lot happier if we just did winter and summer solstice or if we just had a few more traditions that weren't
sentences.zh: 我觉得如果我们能过冬至和夏至，或者多一些不以

sentences.en: marked by spending money, but about connecting to the natural world and connecting to the things around us.
sentences.zh: 花钱为目的，而是关于与自然世界和周围事物建立联系的传统，我们大家都会快乐得多。

sentences.en: So any way that you can find a way to do that for yourself, I think will benefit you deeply and psychologically.
sentences.zh: 所以，任何你能找到的为自己创造仪式感的方法，我认为都会在心理上让你受益匪浅。

sentences.en: That is what every single piece of research I have read on this has said.
sentences.zh: 这是我读过的每一篇相关研究都得出的结论。

sentences.en: It is so rare to find a research area in psychology or anywhere that's like, oh no, we all agree that this is important.
sentences.zh: 在心理学或其他任何领域，很难找到一个大家一致认为“哦，不，我们都同意这很重要”的研究领域。

sentences.en: This is one of those areas.
sentences.zh: 这正是其中之一。

sentences.en: Every single human needs something that they do week after week, year after year to feel like, to feel a sense of the passage of time and to feel like they are living within it.
sentences.zh: 每个人都需要一些年复一年、周复一周去做的事情，来感受时间的流逝，并感觉到自己正生活在其中。

sentences.en: So thank you for listening.
sentences.zh: 所以，谢谢大家的收听。

sentences.zh: 感谢Libby在本期节目中对我的帮助。

sentences.zh: 录完这期节目我可能会发短信问她：你最后一章用了什么美甲？

sentences.zh: 因为我觉得这主意真的太棒了。
